title: Under 5 minutes to a deployed LLM endpoint — Audry Hsu, RunPod
talk_summary: A short vendor demo of RunPod's serverless GPU platform: pick a pre-vetted Hub repo (a GitHub repo with a preconfigured Dockerfile), deploy it as an autoscaling HTTP endpoint with vLLM flags, and get a response in under 5 minutes. The only substantive engineering content is the cold-start/always-on worker tradeoff and per-second billing while a worker is active.

takeaways.technique: Scale-to-zero workers with a small always-on warm pool
takeaways.what_they_do: Serverless endpoints autoscale from zero to a max-worker cap, billed only while a worker handles a request; a configurable number of workers are kept always-on with the model already downloaded so they answer immediately.
takeaways.numbers: first request queued ~41s (cold start: container create + model download); execution ~1.5s; max workers set to 15

takeaways.what_they_do: Deployments start from a curated listing that is literally a GitHub repo with a working Dockerfile and env-var knobs, so the operator only tweaks a couple of flags rather than authoring infra.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these are already vetted open-source listings ... there's already the Dockerfile here. It's already preconfigured for you

takeaways.technique: Expose platform ops as agent-ready CLI/SDK instead of docs
takeaways.what_they_do: They ship CLI support and 'skills' so an agent can drive the platform without a human reading the docs; the console demo is explicitly the human-only path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have skills um to help work with RunPod, everything that's ready for your agent so you don't have to read our documents

takeaways.technique: Spend caps and max-concurrency limits per endpoint
takeaways.what_they_do: Each endpoint has an explicit max-worker cap and a spending cap, so bursty load cannot run away with cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can set limits for caps, for spending caps. And you can also configure workers
